name: Treaty with the Delawares, August 3, 1829 (Sandusky band)
nations: Delaware (Lenape) band on the Sandusky River
promises: Article 2: the United States would pay the band $3,000, $2,000 in hand and $1,000 in horses, clothing, provisions and other goods for the journey west.
Article 1 records that the band ceded the three mile square tract on the Sandusky River reserved to them in 1817 and agreed to join their nation west of the Mississippi.
today: No court, Indian Claims Commission or Court of Claims finding about this cession was located. The Commission's Ohio decisions (Docket 13-F) mention the tract only as a grant made in 1817.

openQuestions: treaties.json names the Delaware Nation, Oklahoma, as the present-day tribe. The band agreed to join the Delawares west of the Mississippi; whether the Delaware Tribe of Indians (Bartlesville) or the Delaware Nation is the successor was not settled here.
The Delaware nations' own account of this treaty was not located.
